name: Web Development Fundamentals
subject: web-dev
description: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, DOM APIs and browser fundamentals

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to create a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The (anchor) tag creates hyperlinks. The destination URL goes in the href attribute: text

questions.question: Which CSS property controls the text colour?
questions.explanation: The CSS 'color' property sets the text colour. Example: color: #ff0000;

questions.question: What does the 'typeof' operator return for an array in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, typeof [] returns 'object'. Use Array.isArray() to check specifically for arrays.

questions.question: What is the correct way to select an element with id 'header' in CSS?
questions.explanation: IDs are selected with '#' in CSS. Class selectors use '.'. So #header targets <div id='header'>.

questions.question: Which method adds an element to the end of a JavaScript array?
questions.explanation: array.push(item) adds one or more elements to the end of an array and returns the new length.

questions.question: What does 'async/await' solve in JavaScript?
options: It makes JavaScript code run faster
It handles asynchronous operations in a synchronous-looking style
questions.explanation: async/await is syntactic sugar over Promises, making async code look and feel like synchronous code.

questions.question: What is the CSS Box Model composed of (from inside out)?
questions.explanation: The CSS Box Model layers from inside out: Content → Padding → Border → Margin.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is used to submit form data to create a new resource?
questions.explanation: POST sends data to create a new resource. GET retrieves data, PUT updates, DELETE removes.

questions.question: What does localStorage.setItem('key', 'value') do?
options: Stores data in the browser that persists after tab close
Stores data only for the current session
questions.explanation: localStorage stores key-value data in the browser that persists across sessions. sessionStorage is cleared when the tab closes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'display: flex' in CSS?
options: Enables one-dimensional layout with powerful alignment controls
questions.explanation: Flexbox enables flexible, one-directional (row or column) layouts with automatic distribution of space.

questions.question: What does JSON.parse() do?
options: Converts a JavaScript object to a JSON string
Converts a JSON string to a JavaScript object
questions.explanation: JSON.parse(str) converts a JSON string to a JavaScript object. JSON.stringify(obj) does the reverse.

questions.question: Which HTML5 element is used to define the main navigation links?
questions.explanation: <nav> is the semantic HTML5 element for navigation links. Using semantic elements improves accessibility and SEO.

questions.question: What is event bubbling in JavaScript?
options: Events fire only on the target element
Events propagate upward from child to parent elements
Events propagate downward from parent to child elements
Events are queued and fired in order
questions.explanation: Event bubbling: when an event fires on a child element, it propagates up through its ancestors. Use event.stopPropagation() to prevent it.

questions.question: What does the CSS 'position: absolute' do?
options: Positions element relative to the viewport
Positions element relative to its nearest positioned ancestor
Locks element to top-left of page
Removes element from DOM flow and centers it
questions.explanation: position: absolute removes the element from normal flow and positions it relative to its nearest non-static ancestor.

questions.question: What is the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
options: No difference, both check value only
=== checks value only; == checks value and type
== checks value only; === checks both value and type
=== is used for assignment; == is for comparison
questions.explanation: == does type coercion (1 == '1' is true). === strict equality checks both value AND type (1 === '1' is false).

questions.question: What is a CSS media query used for?
options: Applying styles based on screen size or device type
questions.explanation: Media queries (@media) apply different CSS rules based on conditions like screen width, enabling responsive design.

questions.question: Which JavaScript method is used to select an element by its CSS class?
questions.explanation: document.querySelector('.classname') returns the first matching element. document.querySelectorAll('.classname') returns all.

questions.question: What does 'semantic HTML' mean?
options: HTML that only uses div and span
HTML that uses tags which convey meaning about their content
questions.explanation: Semantic HTML uses meaningful tags like <article>, <section>, <nav>, <aside> that describe the content's purpose.

questions.question: What is the fetch API used for in JavaScript?
options: Fetching files from the local filesystem
Making HTTP requests to a server
questions.explanation: fetch() makes HTTP requests and returns a Promise. It's the modern replacement for XMLHttpRequest.

questions.question: What does 'z-index' control in CSS?
options: The zoom level of an element
The stacking order of overlapping elements
The horizontal position of an element
questions.explanation: z-index controls the stacking order of positioned elements. Higher z-index = appears on top.
